h1: Centara Hotel Hat Yai — A 4-Star Hotel Linked Straight Into Central Mall in Downtown Hat Yai
intro: If you come to Hat Yai mainly to eat, browse the markets and shop, location is everything — and few places beat Centara Hotel Hat Yai, which sits above Central Department Store. You can walk straight from the lobby into the mall without stepping into the sun. This is a long-established Centara 4-star that many reviews call the most sensible downtown pick, within a few minutes' walk of Kim Yong Market and Lee Gardens. The 248-room hotel has an outdoor pool, fitness centre and spa, with rates from approx. THB 1,800/night. It scores 8.7 from over 3,000 reviews and ranks #1 of 108 Hat Yai hotels on Tripadvisor — its draw is location and service, not newness.

body.html: What has kept Centara Hotel Hat Yai in the conversation for years is its direct connection into Central Department Store · step down from the lobby and you walk straight into the mall, with a supermarket, restaurants, a cinema and shops all in one building · for shoppers and foodies that is an edge few other hotels offer, especially on a rainy or scorching day when you never have to head outside · the hotel is also about 4–5 minutes' walk from Kim Yong Market and close to the Lee Gardens area, the centre of Hat Yai's nightlife.

There are 248 rooms in total, ranging from Superior at 25 sqm, Deluxe at 29 sqm and Premium Deluxe at 36 sqm up to an Executive Suite of 76 sqm · most rooms are larger than the typical downtown hotel, with comfortable beds that reviews single out alongside cleanliness · higher floors give a broad view over Hat Yai · every room has free Wi-Fi and air conditioning — though some reviews note the AC can run very cold or be noisy in certain rooms.
"Best location we've ever stayed in Hat Yai — step out of the lift and you're in the mall. Clean rooms, comfy beds, and every single staff member greeted us with a smile. Breakfast was great."

The shared facilities cover what you'd want from a city hotel · an outdoor pool with a jacuzzi and a fitness centre that overlooks it, plus Cense by Spa Cenvaree for a full range of massages and treatments · dining includes Ginger restaurant serving Japanese, Chinese and Thai dishes, the Saneha cafe for buffets, and a Sky Rooftop Lounge Bar for evening drinks with a city view · the Japanese buffet and breakfast come up often in reviews as good value.

Service is what lifts the overall score · many reviews praise the friendly, smiling staff from the front desk to the servers · several guests say that warmth is exactly why they return on every trip to Hat Yai · free parking is another plus for self-drivers, and in a busy downtown where parking is scarce that genuinely helps.

The trade-off to accept is that the hotel is showing its age · some reviews note that carpets, furnishings and decor look dated next to newer hotels in the same district · the pool and sauna are fairly small rather than resort-scale · and there are complaints about a rigid cancellation policy, especially during the late-2025 floods · if you expect a room that feels brand new, dial expectations back a little.

Rates start around THB 1,800/night for a Superior in regular periods, with Deluxe at roughly THB 2,000–2,600 and the Executive Suite from about THB 4,500 depending on the season · over long weekends and festivals, when Malaysian and Singaporean visitors pour into Hat Yai, prices climb quickly and rooms sell out fast · a score of 8.7 from over 3,000 reviews, a #1-of-108 Tripadvisor ranking and a 2025 Travelers' Choice award show this is a downtown choice that guests stay happy with over the long run.

In short, Centara Hotel Hat Yai suits shoppers and foodies, families who want downtown convenience, and business travellers after a dependable hotel close to everything · if location and service matter most, it fits beautifully at an accessible price · but if you're after a sleek new design hotel or a big resort-style pool, look at one of Hat Yai's newer openings instead.

A tip from the reviews: ask for a higher floor for the city view and less street noise · for shopping, use the indoor link into Central rather than walking out to the street — it's cooler and quicker · always book a Free Cancellation rate, as the cheaper rooms have a strict policy · and reserve well ahead over long weekends, when international visitors book the place out.

honestSummary: Centara Hotel Hat Yai is a 4-star city hotel that stands out for its link into Central mall, warm service and downtown value · 248 rooms within a short walk of Kim Yong Market and Lee Gardens, with a pool, fitness centre and spa, from the low thousands of baht · but accept that the hotel is ageing, some interiors look dated, and the pool is small — this is not a sleek new design hotel.
honestChecks: If you expect brand-new rooms and decor — the hotel is ageing, with some dated carpets and furnishings → if newness matters, look at one of Hat Yai's more recently opened hotels.
If you want a big resort-style pool — the pool and sauna here are fairly small, fine for a quick dip → for poolside relaxation choose a resort outside town or by Samila Beach instead.
If your plans are not yet firm — the cheaper rates have a strict cancellation policy → pick a Free Cancellation package and book ahead over long weekends.

faqTitle: Frequently Asked Questions — Centara Hotel Hat Yai

faq.q: Where is Centara Hotel Hat Yai and how do I get there?
faq.a: It's at 3 Sanehanusorn Road in downtown Hat Yai, Songkhla, sitting above Central Department Store with a direct indoor link · it's about 4–5 minutes' walk to Kim Yong Market and close to Lee Gardens · roughly 5 minutes by car from Hat Yai Railway Station and about 25 minutes from Hat Yai Airport (HDY).

faq.q: What are the room rates and room types at Centara Hotel Hat Yai?
faq.a: Rates start around THB 1,800/night for a 25 sqm Superior · Deluxe at 29 sqm runs about THB 2,000–2,600 · Premium Deluxe at 36 sqm and the 76 sqm Executive Suite from about THB 4,500 · prices depend on season and rise quickly on long weekends, so compare a few platforms before booking.

faq.q: Is Centara Hotel Hat Yai really connected to Central mall?
faq.a: Yes · the hotel sits above Central Department Store with a direct indoor link · from the lobby you can walk straight into the mall, with a supermarket, restaurants, a cinema and shops all in one building — the main draw here for shoppers.

faq.q: Who is Centara Hotel Hat Yai best for?
faq.a: It suits shoppers and foodies, families and business travellers who want downtown convenience · it stands out for location and service · it's less ideal for those after a sleek new design hotel or a big resort-style pool.

faq.q: Is the hotel old · what should I know before booking?
faq.a: The hotel is ageing · some reviews note dated carpets, furnishings and decor, and the pool is fairly small · the cheaper rooms have a strict cancellation policy, so a Free Cancellation package is wise · cleanliness, beds and service still score well.

faq.q: What is breakfast and dining like at Centara Hotel Hat Yai?
faq.a: There's Ginger restaurant (Japanese, Chinese and Thai), the Saneha cafe for buffets, and a Sky Rooftop Lounge Bar with a city view · breakfast and the Japanese buffet are frequently praised as good value · some packages include breakfast, so check when booking.
